Modify or Extend Existing RTL:
Fix elaboration blockers first by matching exact expected top module name/ports in-place within the required file path.
When converting search RTL to delete RTL, preserve traversal timing shape and only add targeted delete/output logic to avoid latency regressions.
For packed BST arrays, copy full input arrays before per-node edits, then invalidate the removed node and scrub parent pointers referencing it.
Reset modified outputs and completion/invalid flags in IDLE so post-operation cleanup checks pass deterministically.
Integrate multiple modules into a top mo:
Unblock integration tasks by first creating the exact expected top module/file name and required companion module files so elaboration can start.
When split-module files are required but empty, add compile-safe implementations with consistent INVALID key/pointer encodings across all outputs.
Keep external interface and latency-visible behavior aligned to the harness contract before deeper refactors.
Use staged RTL only and validate with full parameter sweep after first compile fix.
Create new RTL from spec:
Start by creating the exact expected top module/file so elaboration can begin, then lock ports/parameters to the cocotb contract.
For CIC decimators, implement parameterized integrator and comb arrays with explicit reset for every stage/delay element.
Use a clamped decimation-rate path (1..RMAX) and a bounded cycle counter to drive deterministic output-valid timing.
Gate state updates with valid/ready handshakes so accumulation and decimation stay protocol-safe.
Add `timescale` and prioritize compile-safe correctness before deeper functional tuning.
Debug/fix buggy RTL:
Triaging functional RTL failures should start by validating range-condition operators in classification branches (e.g., ASCII bounds).
For Caesar-style transforms, incorrect inequality direction can silently route letters to wrong paths while compile still passes.
Apply minimal condition fixes first, then rerun full regression to confirm uppercase/lowercase and non-alpha passthrough behavior.
